title: POWER fractional exponent uses powf, not Excel's exp(y*ln x)
notes: RESOLVED bit-exact (715/715 live: 315 ground truth + 400 fresh). Excel POWER fractional = exp(y*ln x) via x87 exp/ln with a DOUBLE-ROUNDED product; for y<0 compute the positive power, store to f64, then one x87 double-rounded reciprocal (the 1-ULP residual -- right function, wrong point). Plus |y|==0.5 -> correctly-rounded hardware sqrt (NOT exp(0.5*ln x)); the reference missed this (only tested 0.5 on negative bases), caught by an OxFunc live sweep. Landed in power_kernel via excel_numeric::{excel_pow_positive,excel_x87_recip} + x87::{mul,recip}. Replaces powf. Spec: docs/EXCEL_POWER_SPEC_AND_TEST_CASES.md.
